prefetch_protocol_audit.dispatch_first_key: The first active key identity is requested while the READY descriptor dispatches. Acceptance starts beat0 on the next visible service cycle.
prefetch_protocol_audit.last_event_next_key: The next active key identity is requested while the current key final event is visible. It may be accepted simultaneously with retirement or earlier during a final-event stall.
prefetch_protocol_audit.early_accept_memory: next_key_prefetched_q suppresses a duplicate request after early acceptance and releases the next key directly to load0 when the held final event retires.
prefetch_protocol_audit.backpressure_fallback: If final-event retirement occurs before prefetch acceptance, drain_prefetch_wait_q suppresses service until the same held identity is accepted, then load0 follows.
prefetch_protocol_audit.stall_identity: Directed VCS held initial identity for 7 cycles, final-event lookahead for 6 cycles, and the already-prefetched final event for 4 further cycles with no identity drift or duplicate acceptance.
prefetch_protocol_audit.ready_valid_boundary: Service and prefetch outputs obey ready/valid stability. Ingress is not generic backpressure: presenting a valid semantic request while no fill bank is available is a sticky protocol violation and requires an upstream credit contract.

zero_bubble_audit.scoreboard_definition: After every accepted nonfinal key's last event, the very next cycle must expose the exact next key load beat0, independent of service_ready.
zero_bubble_audit.sva_subset_definition: Observable subset where the final event and next-key prefetch are accepted simultaneously, followed by exact load0.
zero_bubble_audit.interpretation: The 254/254 result is a directed scheduler/interface result conditional on an identity-only prefetch port being ready in time. It is not a payload-memory latency result.

descriptor_and_pingpong_audit.back_to_back_empty_behavior: Two streamed empty descriptors produce descriptor_done high on two consecutive cycles with different base/context identities.
descriptor_and_pingpong_audit.integration_warning: Downstream must count every high cycle, not only rising edges. There is no descriptor_done_ready backpressure.

implementation_gap_audit.critical_interpretation: weight_prefetch_accept proves only acceptance of source/block/context identity. It neither transports 96 INT8 lanes nor proves that three 256-bit payload beats are resident before load0. If synchronous 256-bit reads start at load0, the load2 response arrives in the first-event cycle and requires an unimplemented tail bypass; without it there is an extra bubble.

findings.finding: The 23-bit prefetch handshake transports only source, block and context, and does not define whether accept means request admission or full-vector residency. No 768-bit payload, response-valid latency, three-beat assembly, or residency proof exists, yet scheduler load0 begins immediately after acceptance. With a synchronous 256-bit SRAM whose reads start at load0, beat2 responds in the first-event cycle and needs a tail bypass; otherwise one bubble is mandatory. Therefore the key mechanism intended to protect the 2.5x frontier is not implemented at the datapath boundary.
findings.required_action: Freeze accept as either full 768-bit residency or add payload-complete backpressure; implement the three 256-bit responses and load2-to-first-event tail bypass, then rerun the exact descriptor cycle miter with real arbiter/SRAM stalls.

findings.finding: The projection has only 6,237,180 cycles of headroom, or 0.754075 extra cycles per active group. One payload bubble for each of 8,271,296 groups increases candidate cycles to 447,979,495 and lowers the projected ratio from 2.535462 to 2.488648.
findings.required_action: Measure the actual payload-ready duty cycle and contention distribution; do not assume an always-ready prefetch endpoint.

findings.finding: Neither a 768-bit lane-vector memory nor its three 256-bit transfers and shared payload arbitration are present. The three counted load beats carry only beat identity, not read request/data/response; port conflicts, bank conflicts, response ordering, tail bypass and energy are uncharged.
findings.required_action: Instantiate a concrete synchronous macro-facing payload path and replay simultaneous PWP/correction demand under arbitration, including the beat2 response boundary.

findings.finding: Service outputs contain load/event identity and negate only. PWP/correction numeric mapping and signed20 accumulator updates are not produced or checked.
findings.required_action: Build an integer-exact token-to-delta mapper and miter every service event into the accumulator input.

findings.finding: The dual presence/direction transpose is 196,608 logical bits expressed as unpacked arrays. No target macro, latency/RDW mode, floorplan, STA or PTPX proves that the W384 scheduler is physically viable.
findings.required_action: Map the bitmap to foundry-supported banks and rerun cycle/physical verification with actual read latency.

findings.finding: M117 validates a standalone scheduler transition kernel, not all heldout descriptor records, payload delivery, numeric accumulation, commit or a matched baseline. The 2.535462 value remains M109 software projection only.
findings.required_action: Execute the exact heldout descriptor/payload trace through the integrated RTL and preserve separate projected, scheduled and physical tiers.

findings.finding: If both descriptor banks are unavailable, presenting event_valid is audited as a sticky illegal request instead of conventional valid-held ready/valid backpressure.
findings.required_action: Freeze a credit-qualified upstream contract or add a skid/credit adapter and charge its storage and cycles.

findings.finding: Two consecutive empty descriptors produce descriptor_done high on adjacent cycles while base/context changes. A rising-edge-only consumer loses the second completion, and there is no done_ready backpressure.
findings.required_action: Specify descriptor_done as a per-cycle valid with mandatory sampling, or add valid/ready buffering and verify downstream consumption.

findings.finding: The direct SVA property observes simultaneous final-event/prefetch acceptance, 246 matches in the independent run; the 254/254 total is completed by procedural scoreboard coverage of early-prefetch cases.
findings.suggested_action: Add a small monitor bit or formal auxiliary state so one assertion covers both simultaneous and early-accepted prefetch paths.

findings.finding: Seeded random, reverse sparse, empty and repeated-stall vectors are strong directed evidence but not exhaustive proof across all descriptor and ready sequences.
findings.suggested_action: Formally prove no duplicate/skip and stable lookahead identity over bounded two-key transitions if a commercial formal slot becomes available.

findings.finding: descriptor_done carries base/context/empty but not valid_rows, accumulator drain completion or partition-431 commit acknowledgement.
findings.suggested_action: Keep scheduler completion distinct from accumulator commit and freeze final partial-window semantics.

findings.finding: service_destination_row is a 12-bit base-plus-offset result, while the interface accepts any 12-bit base. Workload-legal base bounds are not asserted, so high bases can wrap modulo 4096.
findings.suggested_action: Assert the frozen partition base set or widen/check destination arithmetic.

findings.finding: Ingress already consists of unique accepted events. Duplicate removal, PWP assignment, descriptor construction and delivery storage are outside this module and its cycle count.
findings.suggested_action: Name the result a precompacted service-island schedule and keep upstream costs explicit.
